name: share_file
description: Share a file of your worktree with the person, so that they can see it or download it: an image, a chart, an export, a report, a log, anything they asked for as a result that is a file rather than words. Make the file first (write_file, or a command that produces it), then share it with its `path` relative to the root of the worktree. Do not use it for what fits in your answer (a few lines or a short table: write them there), for a file that goes into the pull request (the person reads it there), or to arrange things on the screen (that is `show`). The person gets the file in the conversation: an image is drawn, any other file has its name, its size and a download. Do not paste its contents into your reply, and say in a sentence what it is. For an image the result gives its sha256: `show` draws it in an `Image` block, and an `ask_user` option can carry it as its picture. The file may be at most 4 MiB, and a task may share at most 6 MiB in all. Nothing inside `.git`, and nothing that a symlink leads out of the worktree to, can be shared. Share a file again after you change it. Example: {"path": "out/latency.svg", "name": "Latency by release"}.

path.description: Path of the file, relative to the root of the worktree (no `..`, nothing inside `.git`)

repo.description: The slot the file is in: its name, or the repository's address. Leave out when the workspace has one.

name.description: What the person sees it called. Leave out to use the file's own name.
